root_idea.summary: The root expresses vigilant observation and protection, with distinct lexical branches for herbage and for the kidney or related bodily forms.
root_idea.development: The vigilance branch develops into guarding, watchfulness, cautious self-preservation, deferred payment monitored until due, and sheltered mooring. A separate branch denotes pasture or herbage; the bodily branch and its figurative extensions are recorded as distinct root material.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested Form I verb is displayed under its normalized perfect-tense dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: To guard, protect, or keep safe.
senses.usage_conditions: In the attested Quranic construction, the verb asks who can protect people by night and day from the Merciful; it is transitive with the protected party as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act as a scout or lookout for a party.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional use for performing lookout duty on behalf of a group or people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To keep turning one's eye toward something; to watch or observe it attentively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of repeatedly looking at a thing, or watching a star to see when it rises.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To postpone or be postponed; to defer a debt or its payment, and, of a lifetime, to be prolonged or brought to its delayed end.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source applies the delay branch to debts, payments, and lifetime duration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To beat with a whip.
Of a she-camel, to eat herbage; of land, to contain or abound in herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject determines the construction: an animal grazes, while land is described as rich in pasture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring a ship alongside a riverbank and moor it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of positioning a vessel at a bank or sheltered mooring place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To retain, detain, or confine a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from keeping a ship in place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come to a place and stop, or to come to a person concerning an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe stopping at a place, especially one sheltered from the wind, or approaching someone about a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look into or consider something attentively; to regard someone attentively and be pleased with him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may take an affair as its object or a person who is being examined attentively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pay in advance for corn, food, or similar goods.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The payment precedes delivery of the purchased food or other goods.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To watch or observe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III reciprocal or intensive-derived usage of watching.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an eye sleepless or wakeful; of an eye, to remain wakeful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source records both a causative use with the eye as object and an intransitive use of the eye's wakefulness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring a person's lifetime to its close.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a person's lifetime as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To buy or take something on credit, or to seek a deferment of payment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage concerns taking goods under deferred payment or asking that the payment period be extended.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To guard oneself against someone or something; to be cautious or vigilant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: With an eye as subject, it means to remain wakeful, vigilant, or cautious.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To receive an earnest or money paid in advance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb takes كُلْأَةً in the cited construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh or dry herbage or pasture used as fodder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun for vegetation eaten by livestock; it is reported as having no fixed singular, though كَلَاءٌ is also given as a singular form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deferment or credit arrangement, especially the postponement of a debt's payment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term belongs to the vocabulary of deferred payment and is also used for taking goods on credit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An earnest or money paid in advance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is distinguished in the lexical evidence from its related sense of deferred payment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rich in pasture; of land, containing or abounding in herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One reported specialization describes land whose pasture has been sufficient to satiate its camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a strong, sleepless, or wakeful eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe an eye itself or a person or camel characterized by such an eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A riverbank station or sheltered place where ships are brought and moored; also the bank of a river.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The place is associated with shelter from wind and the safe keeping of vessels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression of walking on the riverbank, an idiomatic image for openly committing calumny and incurring the full prescribed punishment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative conventional expression built on the literal riverbank sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deferred debt or deferred payment; a postponement, including payment for food made at a later period.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In الكالِئُ بالكالِئِ, the expression refers to exchanging one deferred debt or obligation for another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An earnest or money paid in advance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a distinct commercial use from the deferred-payment sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Longer or longest; more or most protracted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjective used especially of duration or the length of life.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An eye constantly fixed upon a person or thing, as when watching it with interest or pleasure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participial expression describes the object of sustained, appreciative attention.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Inflectional and poetic-form commentary; no separate lexical meaning.
